_comment: L2 arg-shape-gate contract. Two deterministic gates turn a would-be validation error into a clarify: `required_args_clarify` (the model omitted something only the user can supply) and `unsupported_args_clarify` (an arg no known tool can express — the inventory-gap case of the reject/clarify taxonomy). Both were Python-only until 2026-09-15, and the L4 lane measured the cost: ffmpeg's `extract_audio` slice sat at 0.872 natively against 0.949 in Python, one row of which was exactly `Tool 'adjust_volume' has unsupported args: [target_sample_rate]` erroring where Python clarified. Consumed by python/core/tests/test_arg_gate_parity.py and `arg_gate_parity_cases` in native/crates/knaif-core/tests/parity.rs.
_stage: Each gate is tested on its own, because they are not composed: `required_args_clarify` runs BEFORE validation and short-circuits (a corrective re-prompt would invite the model to invent the value the user never gave), while `unsupported_args_clarify` runs only AFTER a repair retry has been spent (an undeclared arg is worth one re-prompt; only once that fails is it an inventory gap). Given (plan, registry) each must return the same clarify payload, or None, on both runtimes. Inputs are already normalized: the caller runs normalize_plan + apply_defaults first, so arg aliases are resolved and a merely-misnamed key never reaches here.
_expected_values: `expected` is the clarify payload both runtimes must produce, or null for 'pass through, let validation decide'. Question text is compared exactly: it is the only thing the user sees, and two runtimes phrasing the same refusal differently is a fork.

registries.volume:
adjust_volume:
  description: Adjust volume.
  required_args: [inputs]
  optional_args: [normalize, level]
clarify:
  description: Ask for clarification.
  required_args: [question]
registries.rotate:
rotate_video:
  description: Rotate a video.
  required_args: [input]
  optional_args: [angle, flip]
  any_of_args: [angle, flip]

args.question: I can't adjust volume with target_sample_rate — that isn't supported. Could you rephrase?
I can't adjust volume with bitrate and target_sr — that isn't supported. Could you rephrase?
What angle or flip should I use?
